name: @openrig/studio-cutdown
description: The cutdown provider: punch in/out on a folder of footage, and the lane that renders the cuts. Point --footage at any folder of video.

openrig._note: DECLARED, not discovered — same principle as the video provider. Every hardcoded path removed from this tree existed because there was nowhere to state it.

processes._note: TWO processes, and the second is not optional. The server ACCEPTS cuts; the lane PERFORMS them. Run the server alone and every write verb answers ok:true while nothing ever renders — accepted-but-unperformed, which passes both a verbs-answer check and a real-data check because the job file genuinely gains a line.

args.--footage: required; the folder of video being cut down
args.--bundle: optional; where renders land, defaults to <footage>

args.--interval: optional; sweep period in ms, default 10000

lane.history: Rewritten from watch-markers.sh, which used `stat -c %Y` — GNU syntax. On macOS that returned nothing, the guard fell through, and the cut lane never ran at all. It was Linux-only by accident.

footage.description: any folder of video files. A proxies/ subdir is used when present (review proxies) and originals/ is preferred as the cut source when present, but a plain folder works — that is the whole setup.

bundle.description: where cut clips are written; defaults to the footage root so the tool is self-contained

ffmpeg.used_for: cutting clips to in/out, stabilization passes

ffprobe.used_for: clip duration for the stabilize progress readout

state._note: Append-only and attributed, written into the footage root. Durable-first: the UI gesture lands on disk before anything renders.
state.markers.jsonl: punch in/out marks, attributed by UI user

_deps_note: The cut lane shells out to ffmpeg/ffprobe. Shipped with the provider so a box needs only node — see studio-video/timeline-export-probe.mjs resolveSystemBin for the packaged-first, PATH-fallback order.
